 Families of wrongfully detained Americans hope Trump raises their loved ones' cases
 By Jennifer Hansler 
 The families of two Americans designated as wrongfully detained in China are hopeful President Donald Trump will raise the plights of their loved ones during his visit.
 Min Zin is an American academic who was detained in June. In a statement, his wife Sylvia said he is being held “on false charges at an undisclosed location in solitary confinement without any access to legal counsel.”
 She is increasingly worried about her husband’s health and “recently learned that Min Zin was hospitalized last month for severe dehydration due to stomach illness and that there is no heat in the location he is being held.”
 She said she is “grateful for the President’s commitment in continuing to raise my husband’s wrongful detention and his work to secure Min Zin’s immediate and unconditional release.”
 “My daughter and I remain hopeful in the President’s ability to bring him home to us in time for the holidays. Min Zin should be with his family,” Sylvia Zin said.
 Youlin Chen , a seismologist, was detained in November 2024. Advocates say he is being used as a political pawn.
 His wife, Yufang Rong said in a statement that she has “been assured that President (Donald) Trump remains firmly committed to securing Youlin’s freedom and that he intends to raise Youlin’s case with President Xi at both the APEC meeting and, if needed, the G20.”
 “We all know that when President Trump gets involved, Americans come home,” she said.
 “I am not worried about his trial. He has already spent two years in prison without committing a crime,” she said. Chen had a trial last month.
 Trump told reporters talks “a lot” with the Xi about detained Americans. A senior US official said that “resolving the wrongful detentions of US citizens is always a top priority for the president.”
 In addition to the two Americans who have been designated as wrongfully detained, there are other Americans detained in China haven’t been designated, including Nelson Wells and Dawn Hunt, as well as a number of Americans who have been blocked from leaving the country due to exit bans.

 Ukrainian negotiating team will be updated on Trump's China meetings, Zelensky says
 By Hira Humayun and Victoria Butenko 
 US officials said they would update Ukraine’s negotiating team in Berlin about President Donald Trump’s efforts in China, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday.
 “US officials said that during our meetings in Berlin, they would provide the necessary information about the US President’s ongoing negotiations, including those currently taking place in China,” the Ukrainian leader said.
 As Trump meets his Chinese and Russian counterparts in China, where he is expected to discuss the war in Ukraine, the “Coalition of the Willing” are holding a meeting in Berlin on the same subject.
 Zelensky said other Ukrainian allies will also be providing information from China.
 “We will receive information from China, as well as from other countries and other leaders—our partners,” he said.

 Trump and Carney met on sidelines of APEC summit
 By Max Saltman 
 US President Donald Trump discussed ongoing trade negotiations with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, according to a readout from Carney’s office.
 The two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement that would create good jobs, boost affordability, and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture, and sovereignty,” Carney’s office said.
 After Trump launched a trade war with Canada in 2025, Carney quickly sought to strengthen Canadian relationships with Europe and Asia. The prime minister announced a trade deal with China yesterday, and plans to launch a new trade mission to China next year.

 As Trump meets Putin and Xi, Witkoff and Kushner are due in Europe for Ukraine talks
 By Sebastian Shukla and Billy Stockwell 
 As US President Donald Trump meets with his Russian and Chinese counterparts in China on Thursday, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to attend Ukraine talks in Germany, according to a German government official.
 Kyiv made a familiar appeal earlier on Wednesday ahead of Trump’s meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, asking that no decisions should be made about Ukraine without its participation. Trump said earlier this week the trio would discuss Ukraine.
 On Thursday, Witkoff and Kushner – Trump’s son-in-law who acts as one of the country’s top diplomats despite holding no official role within the Trump administration – will join a meeting of the “Coalition of the Willing” to discuss the Ukraine war, the German official said.
 The US envoys will meet with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz at the start of the meeting, which is being co-hosted by Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the official said. The pair will join a news conference later in the day alongside Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the official added.
 The timing of the coalition meeting has been carefully choreographed by Germany – Ukraine’s biggest financial supporter – to allow Kyiv’s European allies to respond quickly and act on outcomes from Shenzhen, the official said.
 Remember: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said earlier Wednesday that the US and China should use Thursday’s talks to pressure Russia into ending the nearly five-year war, given both countries have a “decisive influence” over Moscow.
 The expected meeting in Berlin comes amid a flurry of renewed diplomacy over Ukraine. Witkoff and Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Putin last week after US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi concluded with no clear breakthrough.

 Trump will have one-on-one meeting with Putin on Thursday in China, US official confirms
 By Kit Maher 
 US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. 
 Reuters/Getty Images 
 A US official confirmed that President Donald Trump will have a one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in China.
 Trump’s last in-person meeting with Putin was on US soil in Alaska in August 2025. The summit yielded no significant movement toward peace in Russia’s war on Ukraine – something that Trump has been trying to achieve since the start of his second term.
 Putin was quick to shake hands with Trump ahead of the family photo at the APEC Summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday night, which was captured on video.

 Trump greets Putin and Xi ahead of high-stakes meeting. Catch up on today's events
 By Catherine Nicholls 
 US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin gather before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China on Wednesday. 
 Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press/AP 
 US President Donald Trump is now in Shenzhen, one of China’s most populous cities, after waking up this morning in the Philippines. He was greeted at the airport by Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier today, a first for Xi in his current role.
 Elsewhere: 
 Trump began the day in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, where he sat down with his counterpart Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for a meeting. Trump said the two countries would probably do “something big” on nuclear power.
 The US president then traveled to Shenzhen in China. He was met at the airport by Xi in what was a rare move. According to China’s diplomatic protocol in recent years, the head of state generally doesn’t go to the airport to greet guests.
 Later, Trump met separately with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Sheinbaum called it a “very good meeting.” 
 At the site of this year’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit., Trump shook hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin . When Trump arrived, a band played “America the Beautiful.” He briefly stopped to enjoy the music, clapping lightly and pumping his fist.
 During his banquet speech at the summit, Xi spotlighted the “extraordinary” transformation of Shenzhen , which has become a “city of innovation” from a small fishing village in only a few decades.
 Meanwhile, earlier in the day, Putin said he expects “considerable potential benefits” from his scheduled meeting tomorrow with Xi and Trump, Russian state media TASS reported.
 CNN’s Kathleen Magramo, Sylvie Zhuang, Veronica Calderon, Lauren Kent, Kit Maher, Yong Xiong, Billy Stockwell and Lex Harvey contributed to this reporting.

 As Trump, Putin and Xi prepare to meet, Ukraine issues a familiar plea
 By Billy Stockwell and Daria Tarasova-Markina 
 Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha delivers a speech during a press briefing in Bucharest, Romania, on November 5. 
 Inquam Photos/Octav Ganea/Reuters 
 US President Donald Trump said earlier this week he intends to discuss the Ukraine war with his Russian and Chinese counterparts on Thursday, despite earlier suggestions by US officials that the topic wouldn’t be on the table.
 Kyiv — no doubt cautious about what might be discussed or agreed during the meeting — has made a familiar appeal: No decisions should be made about Ukraine without its participation.
 Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Wednesday the US and China should use Thursday’s talks to pressure Russia into ending the nearly five-year war, given both countries have a “decisive influence” on Moscow.
 “It is important that, through this meeting, these two global leaders do not give Putin the false impression of a return to the era of spheres of influence,” Sybiha said, according to Ukrainian state media outlet Ukrinform. “The tone must be different – pressure on Putin, and they have that pressure to bring this war to an end.”
 Putin said on Wednesday he expects “considerable potential benefits ” from the trilateral talks, Russian state media TASS reported.
 Alongside the trilateral meeting, Trump and Putin are also expected to speak separately during this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, according to Russian officials.
 More context : The talks come amid renewed US efforts to end the war in Ukraine. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russia’s Vladimir Putin last week after US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi concluded with no clear breakthrough.
 CNN’s Kevin Liptak and Lex Harvey contributed reporting.

 Why Xi may not hold talks with Japan’s leader in China
 By Jessie Yeung 
 Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi shakes hands with China’s President Xi Jinping before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday. 
 Iori Sagisawa/Reuters 
 Last October, Chinese leader Xi Jinping sat down for a meeting with Japan’s newly elected prime minister Sanae Takaichi. The two countries should be “partners, not threats” to each other, Xi told her.
 One year later, that hopeful statement has long been forgotten. China-Japan relations remain strained – with no sign the two leaders will hold a formal talk at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit this week.
 Takaichi arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday for her first visit to China since taking office. She was greeted by a retired Chinese diplomat in a colder than usual reception at the airport, according to Japanese media’s coverage of the meeting.
 Takaichi and Xi met at the welcome banquet in the evening, where Xi nodded to her as they shook hands. It’s unclear what Takaichi said to Xi.
 Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping shake hands at the welcome banquet of the APEC meeting in Shenzhen. 
 Reuters 
 Their spat began just weeks after that first meeting when Takaichi suggested Japan could respond militarily if China were to move to take control of self-ruled Taiwan by force. China’s Communist Party claims Taiwan as its own territory, despite never having controlled it.
 Taiwan is one of China’s red lines – and Beijing was furious that Takaichi crossed it. Since then, China has put economic pressure on Japan, warning its citizens not to travel there; nationalist and anti-Japanese fervor spread on Chinese social media; and dozens of Japanese performers canceled performances in China, even if they didn’t cite the diplomatic row as a reason.
 When asked whether Xi would meet with Takaichi at APEC, a Chinese Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesperson gave a terse response.
 “As to China-Japan relations, we have made clear our position more than once.”
 That position is evident in a quick glance through the ministry’s briefings this past year.
 In November, it warned Japan: “Stop crossing the line and playing with fire.” In December: “We once again urge the Japanese side to reflect on and correct its wrongdoings.” Then in March: “Time for Japan to stop going further down the wrong path.”
 The countries have a long history of animosity. In the early 20th century, Japan’s Imperial Army invaded China and committed war crimes – including the Nanjing massacre . Japan has repeatedly apologized for the atrocities, but they remain a sharp pain point.

 Here's what happened the last time Trump and Xi met in the US
 By Catherine Nicholls 
 US President Donald Trump greets Chinese President Xi Jinping during an arrival ceremony at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, on September 23. 
 Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images 
 In an extremely rare move for China’s top leader, Xi Jinping met US President Donald Trump at the airport in Shenzhen earlier, ahead of an APEC banquet today and a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin tomorrow.
 Xi said he greeted Trump at the airport to reciprocate after Trump personally greeted Xi when he arrived at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland earlier this year.
 In September, Xi took part in his first visit to the US capital in more than a decade, visiting for three days alongside his wife, Peng Liyuan.
 During the trip, the two leaders extended a trade truce, exchanged gifts and compliments, and acknowledged the possibility of working together to contain the dangers of AI development.
 Trump gave Xi a tour of a new helipad on the South Lawn and a look inside Marine One during his time at the White House. He then held a state dinner with guests including then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and OpenAI President and Co-Founder Greg Brockman.
 At the White House state dinner, Xi emphasized the importance of cooperation, in remarks that framed China’s rise as a boon to America rather than a threat.
 “The friendship between the two peoples is a worthy cause that holds great promise,” he said. “Let us join hands and move forward side by side.”
 In his speech, Trump also detailed a long history of trade and friendship between the US and China.
 “President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure. We’ve never gotten along better,” he said.

 Xi spotlights China's “modernization” in APEC banquet speech
 By Yong Xiong and Billy Stockwell 
 China's President Xi Jinping speaks at a welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Wednesday. 
 Maxim Shemetov/Reuters 
 Chinese leader Xi Jinping used his banquet speech on Wednesday evening to spotlight the “extraordinary” transformation of the high-tech city of Shenzhen — which is hosting this week’s APEC summit — from a small fishing village to a “city of innovation.”
 He said the city’s transformation has been “nothing short of extraordinary” and represents a “frontier” in Chinese innovation.
 “Shenzhen’s story is a microcosm of China’s reform and opening up,” and showcases the “many facets of Chinese modernization,” Xi said, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.
 “When I first visited Shenzhen in 1978, it was still a small fishing village. More than 40 years have passed in the blink of an eye. Today, skyscrapers tower over the city, and its streets bustle with traffic,” Xi told guests at a welcome banquet for the summit.
 The Chinese president said he hoped for “tangible results” as a result of Thursday’s Economic Leaders’ meeting.
 “We will discuss measures to further open up to one another, explore pathways for innovation-driven growth, expand opportunities for practical cooperation across various fields, and work to translate more initiatives into tangible results,” CCTV cited Xi as saying.

 Trump is the first sitting US president to visit Shenzhen, China's "miracle city"
 By Sylvie Zhuang 
 Members of the public watch an APEC themed light show at the summit square of Lianhuashan Park in Shenzhen on Tuesday night. 
 Zhang Xiangyi/China News Service/VCG/Getty Images 
 Donald Trump has become the first sitting US president to land in Shenzhen, China’s preeminent tech metropolis which has more billionaires than any city outside New York.
 During his visit, Chinese leader Xi Jinping will be able to show off the urban microcosm of his nation’s modern story: high-level planning, roaring technological advancement, and rapid wealth creation.
 A stone’s throw from Hong Kong, Shenzhen is China’s answer to Silicon Valley; a futuristic city that’s home to tech entrepreneurs, food-delivering drones and the world’s fastest supercomputer.
 It’s a city that launched many of the tech advances that have put Trump and Xi on a collision course over access to raw materials, advanced chips, and lucrative markets. (A fragile trade truce between the world’s two biggest economies will expire in January.)
 And it’s quickly becoming one of China’s top destinations for foreign travelers.
 If you chat with any of Shenzhen’s 18 million people, they will proudly tell you it is a “miracle city.”
 Fifty years ago – around the time a bullish young Trump was inking his first Manhattan real-estate deal – this city did not exist.
 Built out of mangrove wetlands over just four decades, the gleaming city boasts more skyscrapers than New York City and roughly three times more than Chicago, according to the Council on Vertical Urbanism.
 Walking through its streets, everything feels brand new. Self-driving electric taxis purr quietly along the roads, while drones fly around delivering hot meals and iced coffee. Crystal-like orbs dangle from roadside trees, collecting solar energy and illuminating the streets at night.

 Trump arrives at APEC welcome banquet in China, shakes hands with Putin
 By Kit Maher 
 US President Donald Trump shakes hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as Chinese leader Xi Jinping stands beside them before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. 
 Iori Sagisawa/Reuters 
 President Donald Trump shook hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin shortly after his arrival at a welcome banquet for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, leaders in Shenzhen, China.
 The world leaders all walked through a red carpeted entrance way upon their arrival at the event. When Trump arrived, a band of strings and woodwinds played “America the Beautiful.” He briefly stopped to enjoy the music, clapping lightly and pumping his fist, before turning to face the cameras head-on for photographs.
 Each leader was introduced on the speakers and walked up to shake hands with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, who are hosting the gathering.
 After Xi greeted each leader individually, they all gathered for a photo. Putin quickly approached Trump and the two leaders shook hands and exchanged a few words.
 Putin, Xi and Trump pose for a family photo with other world leaders ahead of the APEC summit dinner. 
 Russian pool 
 Among the leaders gathering are Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, both of whom Trump met with, according to a White House official.

 What is APEC and why are the world’s leaders gathering in Shenzhen?
 By Jessie Yeung 
 China's President Xi Jinping, center, poses for a group photo with other leaders before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday. 
 Iori Sagisawa/AFP/Getty Images 
 Leaders from around the world – heads of state, business executives, policymakers and more – are gathering in Shenzhen this week for the annual summit of a group known as APEC.
 The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) is a 21-member bloc that includes major Pacific Rim economies like the United States, Canada, Australia, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea and more. The grouping represents 61% of the world’s total GDP and 47% of global trade, according to the Office of the United States Trade Representative. 
 They take turns hosting the summit each year, where representatives discuss trade, industry, and regional tensions and security.
 This year China is hosting, with the summit held in the southern tech and manufacturing hub just across the border from Hong Kong.
 There are several events on the calendar, but people will be most closely watching the Economic Leaders’ meeting today and tomorrow, where heads of state will gather and hold potentially consequential talks on the sidelines.
 Past APEC summits have proved consequential – in 2018, for instance, US and Chinese leaders each delivered strongly-worded speeches as tensions rose between the two powers, with the bloc failing to agree on a joint communique for the first time in its 25-year history. Last year, Trump skipped APEC – but held a meeting with Xi just beforehand where they reached a trade deal after months of battling tariffs.

 Will Putin and Trump hold separate talks in China?
 By Billy Stockwell and Arina Porkhovnik
 US President Donald Trump speaks with Russian President Vladimir Putin at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska, on August 15, 2025. 
 Kevin Lamarque/Reuters/File 
 US President Donald Trump will meet on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, during unprecedented trilateral talks together with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
 But that is not the only occasion Trump and Putin will cross paths in the city.
 The Russian leader spoke briefly with Trump at a gala reception for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit guests on Wednesday evening local time.
 Kremlin foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said Wednesday the pair could also meet tomorrow for separate talks.
 “There will be a meeting, there will be. And I believe that our president and the president of the United States will speak several times over the course of APEC,” Ushakov told Russian state media outlet Vesti.
 Their meeting will be an “intimate affair” without the involvement of large delegations, Vesti cited Ushakov as saying.
 Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said there is unlikely to be an opportunity for “full-format talks” between the US and Russian leaders, Russian state media TASS said.
 He did however say the pair will likely discuss the Ukraine conflict and possibly Iran, TASS reported.

 Trump greeted at airport by Xi in extremely rare move ahead of meeting with Putin. Catch up
 By Catherine Nicholls 
 President Trump arrives in Shenzhen, China

 US President Donald Trump is now in Shenzhen, China, where he was greeted at the airport by Chinese leader Xi Jinping, a first for Xi in his current role.
 Historically, it is extremely rare for China’s top leader to personally welcome foreign leaders upon their arrivals.
 Trump is expected to take part in an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) banquet this evening, then several significant meetings tomorrow. 
 Here’s the latest: 
 Upon his arrival in China, Trump was greeted by enthusiastic spectators, a military flyover, an honor guard, and Xi. The Chinese leader said he met Trump at the airport to reciprocate after Trump personally greeted Xi when he arrived at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland earlier this year.
 Before this, Trump had a short stop in Manila, the Philippines. He touted a potential nuclear energy deal with the Philippines as he sat down with his counterpart Ferdinand Marcos Jr, and said that he was not worried about tensions between Manila and Beijing over the South China Sea.
 Meanwhile, during a meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the authoritarian leaders of Russia and China touted the stability of their relationship and its benefit to the world order.
 Russian President Vladimir Putin said he expects “considerable potential benefits” from his scheduled meeting with Trump and Xi tomorrow, Russian state media TASS reported.

 Trump to see why US efforts won't stop China's rise as tech behemoth
 Analysis by Simone McCarthy in Beijing
 The skyline in Shenzhen, China, is lit up for the upcoming APEC Summit on November 16, 2026. 
 Kevin Frayer/Getty Images 
 For Xi Jinping, a summit in the high-tech hub of Shenzhen this week is an opportune moment to showcase a vision of China’s unrelenting rise.
 Xi is hosting business moguls and world leaders for an annual regional economic summit, where he’ll sit down to sideline talks with US President Donald Trump and hold a three-way meeting with Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, a first-ever trilateral for the nuclear-armed powers.
 And for his backdrop, Xi has chosen a host city that’s synonymous with China’s rapid transformation into a high-tech powerhouse — and its resilience in the face of US tech and trade frictions.
 A sprawling metropolis of 18 million, Shenzhen is home to a who’s-who of Chinese tech titans: hardware giant Huawei, dronemaker DJI and the Tesla-beating electric vehicle seller BYD — all companies that have thrived despite US import bans or blacklists.
 Once known as the capital of luxury knockoffs and cheap electronics, today the city’s high-tech products have helped propel China’s export juggernaut to a record $1 trillion trade surplus already this year.
 Visiting VIPs who step out onto Shenzhen’s streets this week will find traffic that moves to the whir of homegrown electric vehicles and novelty kiosks where robots serve up coffee. Self-driving taxis ferry passengers and drones deliver take-out in some areas. Surveillance cameras are ubiquitous.
 The high-tech vision may make for a sharp contrast to the US , where news this week has been dominated by a series of systems outages and a revelation that up until a few months ago the country’s aviation administration was still using floppy disks.

 By Catherine Nicholls 
 US President Donald Trump arrives at his hotel in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. 
 Pedro Pardo/AFP/Getty Images 
 US President Donald Trump is now in Shenzhen, China, after spending part of the day in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, during his ongoing Asia tour.
 Here’s a look at his remaining schedule: 
 Wednesday
 Trump was greeted at the airport in Shenzhen by Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who has never before gone to the airport to receive a visiting US president while in his current position.
 In a Xinhua news agency readout of Xi’s remarks to Trump, the Chinese leader said he was reciprocating after Trump met him at the airport when he visited the US earlier this year.
 At his hotel, Trump is set to hold meetings with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, according to the White House press pool.
 The president is also expected to take part in a photo alongside Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders, which will be followed by a banquet.
 Thursday
 Tomorrow, Trump is expected to take part in an APEC conference session.
 He will then meet with Xi.
 Later in the day, he is also scheduled to take part in a meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. 
 Following this, Trump is scheduled to travel back to the White House.

 By Sylvie Zhuang 
 US President Donald Trump walks alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrives at Shenzhen Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders Summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. 
 Carlos Barria/Reuters 
 Arriving in China for his second visit this year, Trump was greeted by enthusiastic spectators, a military flyover, an honor guard – and an embrace from Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
 When Trump exited Air Force One, he was greeted by rows of young women and men wearing pink and baby blue who were holding flowers and shouting “Welcome!”
 Xi and Trump embraced each other at the bottom of the steps. A girl handed Trump a bouquet of flowers, and then the US president shook hands with top communist party leaders one by one.
 Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes US President Donald Trump.

 Trump is presented by flowers upon arrival.

 A People’s Liberation Army (PLA) honor guard was present and five military jets flew over the airport, leaving pink, blue and yellow smoke trails in the sky.
 In a Xinhua readout of Xi’s remarks to Trump, the Chinese leader remembered how the US president and his wife made a “special trip to the airport to greet me, and a grand welcome ceremony was held,” referring to his trip to the US earlier this year.
 Trump greets people as Xi looks on.

 “China is a nation of courtesy, with a tradition of reciprocity,” the readout quoted Xi as saying.
